conviction_note: Peers that reported Jul-Sep quarters after EL last spoke mostly support the travel-retail-led H1 that management already guided, but that thesis is in the guide and in a +16% run-up with a whisper ($0.60) above consensus ($0.50-0.53). The findings net to about -0.3 and the scaled number is +0.36 (p_up 52 x abs 9.0). The two disagree in sign only because both sit inside noise: the evidence is balanced, and the name's reaction distribution (+16.3, -19.2, -16.1 on three of the last seven) says the move will be large in whichever direction the guide and the China tone take it.

findings.finding: L'Oreal's Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep, the same months as EL's fiscal Q1) beat: group LFL +7.7% against 5.9% expected. Travel retail returned to growth with sell-in +10% and sell-out up low to mid single digits. Hainan was 'very positive', North Asia TR was less negative (-MSD), China domestic beauty was about +2-3%, and the CEO put global beauty at ~+5%. That supports EL's guided H1 driver of 'stronger travel retail shipments' (TR ~15% of EL sales), which consensus has at about +4.9% reported growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Travel retail and China have driven EL's biggest reactions: 2025-02-04 -16.07% and 2026-02-05 -19.19% (baseline), versus +16.3% on 2026-08-19, when management said TR turned positive in June/July led by Hainan (Q4 FY26 transcript).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. L'Oreal reported on 2026-10-22, EL closed $108.67 on 10-23 (+0.88%) and has drifted to $106.69. If the TR read-through were fully priced, the 5-day run-up would be positive and the skew more call-bid than -1.7. The ~+5% revenue consensus sits at the middle of the FY organic range even though management said H1 runs ahead of H2. The finding is shrunk because it lands inside a guided H1 driver and covers one segment of ~15% of sales, with the other ~85% (NA, EUKEM, China mainland) needing to hold.
findings.independence: Separate sources: L'Oreal group/North Asia +7.8% and TR 'sustained growth' (Luxury Tribune, https://www.luxurytribune.com/en/loreal-accelerates-growth-in-the-3rd-quarter-of-2026-driven-by-luxury-and-emerging-markets, 2026-10-23); Hainan offshore duty-free H1 2026 +18.8% y/y per Haikou Customs (https://m.gelonghui.com/live/2443334, cited in search); Korea duty-free +15.9% in July (filed separately below). Same direction, different series.

findings.finding: Korea duty-free sales (excluding inflight) rose 15.9% y/y in July 2026 to KRW1.067tn, driven by foreigners (77.3% of sales; airport foreign sales +22.7%, downtown +30.3%). Korea TR was a named driver of EL's FY26 Asia/Pacific growth, and July is EL's fiscal Q1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same TR line as above; no EL-specific reaction to Korean duty-free data on record.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an industry series that sell-side TR models read loosely. One month of data, out two months before the print. It is a proxy, not EL's sell-in, and Korean nationals' purchases fell 13.5%. Small.
findings.independence: Proxy. Independent of the L'Oreal call. EL's FY26 release names Korea and Hong Kong TR and Hainan as APAC drivers (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001001250/000100125026000038/elq4fy2026exhibit991.htm).

findings.finding: China's NBS cosmetics retail sales rose 5.4% y/y in September 2026 to RMB39.0bn and 6.1% for Jan-Sep, while total retail grew only 1.1% (gold/jewellery -9.6%). Cosmetics held up in a weak consumer tape during EL's fiscal Q1. EL's mainland China grew high single digits in FY26 (+7% organic in Q4).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: China has been the swing line in EL's large moves (2025-02-04 -16.07%, 2026-02-05 -19.19%). Q4 FY26 China +7% organic coincided with +16.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a public macro series, so largely priced. It mixes mass and prestige and is not EL's own number. It is filed small as confirmation that the China trend did not break during the quarter. EL's China investor event on Nov 4 means management will want to show China strength.
findings.independence: L'Oreal's CEO put China domestic beauty at about +2-3% for nine months, a weaker figure (https://moodiedavittreport.com/?p=486532). Puig's Asia Pacific grew +12.9% LFL in Q3 (https://moodiedavittreport.com/?p=486411).

findings.finding: Puig's Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep): group LFL +5.6%. Skincare fell 0.8% at constant perimeter, its second straight negative quarter, and management said premium skincare 'remained soft'. Makeup grew +16.1%. EL is the most skin-care-weighted prestige house (Estee Lauder, Clinique, La Mer), so the read is negative for its largest category and positive for MAC/Clinique makeup, which EL guided to return to growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean EL reaction to a skin-care-only surprise in the baseline. Skin care weakness was part of the FY25 sell-offs.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer category data is read by the beauty analysts, so mostly priced. Filed net of the offsetting makeup strength. Circana's H1 2026 US prestige skincare +9% contradicts a broad skincare slump, so this is sized below that series.
findings.independence: Puig's skincare is small (~10% of sales) and partly dermocosmetics. Circana US prestige H1 2026: skincare +9%, makeup +3%, fragrance +6% (https://www.premiumbeautynews.com/en/us-beauty-market-stays-strong-in,28150) points the other way.

findings.finding: LVMH Perfumes & Cosmetics (Dior, Guerlain, Givenchy) grew only ~1% organically in Q3 2026 and was flat over nine months, citing a less buoyant China. Selective Retailing (Sephora) grew +8% organically with share gains. Prestige brand owners other than L'Oreal were soft while the retailer was strong.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. Peer softness in China preceded EL's 2025-02 and 2026-02 drops.
findings.why_not_priced: Released 2026-10-12, before EL's October run toward $108.7, so the market looked through it. It is the counterweight to the L'Oreal read and shows the prestige read-through is not uniform.
findings.independence: Contradicted in part by L'Oreal Luxe +7% (https://www.luxurytribune.com/en/loreal-accelerates-growth-in-the-3rd-quarter-of-2026-driven-by-luxury-and-emerging-markets). Separate document.

findings.finding: Amazon Prime Day 2026 ran June 23-26, in EL's fiscal Q4 FY26. In 2025 it ran in July, inside fiscal Q1 FY26. So Q1 FY27 laps a Prime Day quarter with no event of its own, and Amazon sell-in moved into Q4. Management flagged the shift on the August call but also said July retail in North America was 'extremely strong', led by Clinique and MAC. Net: a modest North America timing headwind against a strong July.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: North America returned to organic growth only in Q4 FY26 (Americas +5% organic), on the print that rose +16.3%. Earnings Whispers names NA sustainability as a key watch point.
findings.why_not_priced: Management mentioned it on the call, so models likely carry some timing. If the market had weighted it, previews would discount the Q1 NA number; the Earnings Whispers preview names NA as a watch point without the timing. Sized small and netted against the 'July extremely strong' comment.
findings.independence: Same management commentary as the July-strength statement: Q4 FY26 transcript (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/EL/Q42026), one document, so merged into one finding. Prime Day dates are independently confirmed (https://thenextweb.com/news/amazon-moves-prime-day-back-to-june-and-keeps-it-a-four-day-event).

findings.finding: The setup carries a raised bar. Shares are up ~16% since the August print (+16.0% over 20 days), near the post-earnings high ($109.35) and well above the 200-day ($91.76). The whisper is $0.60 against a $0.50-0.53 consensus, and bullish sentiment rose to 19.2% from 6.5%. A beat at consensus likely clears less than an in-line guide reiteration costs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 (2025-10-30), a reaffirm after a strong pre-print run, moved +0.26%. Q4 FY25 (2025-08-20) -3.67% and Q3 FY25 -1.78% on in-line prints. Beats with raised guides have paid (+16.3%), misses on China/TR have cost 16-19%.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price itself, so this is not 'unpriced'. It is filed as the bar the print has to clear. Against it: short interest is only 2.0% with 2.5 days to cover, and the skew (-1.7) leans slightly to calls, which is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: Baseline tape (run_up_20d +16.0%, pct_from_52w_high -10.8%). Short interest rose 391k shares into 2026-10-15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/el/shortinterest).

findings.finding: Interparfums' Q3 2026 USD sales were flat at ~$430M. US-based operations fell 7%, mainly on delayed giftset shipments, while Coach rose 23% and Montblanc 12%. The CEO said activity improved over the summer and the company targets the top of FY guidance. This is a soft read on US fragrance sell-in timing for the holiday build.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No EL history on this line. Fragrance is EL's growth category (Le Labo, Tom Ford, Kilian, Jo Malone), but Interparfums is masstige/licensed.
findings.why_not_priced: Off-line peer (masstige licences), widely reported. The decline is a giftset timing issue, not demand. Tiny.
findings.independence: Puig Fragrance & Fashion +3.9% LFL in Q3 (https://moodiedavittreport.com/?p=486411) and L'Oreal naming fragrance its strongest category point the other way.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26 adjusted EPS included a $38M (+$0.07) benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds booked in cost of sales. The FY26 10-K says remaining unsubmitted or unreceived refunds are 'not material', so Q1 FY27 should carry no comparable refund. There is no hidden one-off upside to the $0.50-0.53 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The refund sat inside the +16.3% Q4 print, which traded on guidance, not on the refund.
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed in the 10-K and immaterial by the company's own statement. Filed to close off the refund angle that moved other names; sized 0.
findings.independence: Q4 FY26 release states the $38M benefit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001001250/000100125026000038/elq4fy2026exhibit991.htm). Same company, different document.

baseline_tension: The evidence is near-balanced and does not cut against a small call-leaning skew (-1.7). The positive peer read on travel retail is offset by a +16% run-up and a whisper above consensus, so the sign stays near 50/50 while the magnitude stays at the implied ~9%.
lessons_applied: Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest) and lesson 6 (inside the guide): the L'Oreal travel-retail finding cut from +1.0 to +0.7, because TR is ~15% of sales and H1 TR strength is already in the company's guide.

Lesson 7 (positioning against skew; short interest checked): the raised-bar positioning finding cut from -0.8 to -0.6, because the skew is mildly call-bid and short interest (2.0%, 2.5 days) gives no crowding signal either way.
Lesson 6 (bar): the bar is sourced to three roughly agreeing EPS estimates ($0.50/$0.52/$0.53) and two agreeing revenue estimates (~$3.64-3.65B), so no cap applies.
Lessons 1 and 8 left p_up at 52 and abs_move at 9.0: the name's reaction distribution is wide and the fact-to-reaction link is weak, so the uncertainty sits in p_up, not in a smaller magnitude.
